cds.title: University of New Hampshire Common Data Set 2025-2026 (pdf, published 9.2.26)

scorecard.title: College Scorecard (location, enrollment, cost; data released 2026-10-15)

stats.notes: From the Common Data Set (Fall 2025 entering class, C1): 21,567 applied, 19,224 admitted (89.1%), 2,302 enrolled; residency rows (in-state 4,548 / out-of-state 16,521 / international 498 applicants) add up to the totals. International first-years: 498 applied, 425 admitted (85.3%), 34 enrolled. No early decision, no waitlist; nonbinding Early Action (Nov 15) and regular decision. The GPA breakdown covers all enrolled students; the 4.0 row is the share with a 4.0 GPA, and a further 0.04% had a GPA below 1.0 (left out). Test scores are optional: 446 enrolled students (19.4%) submitted SAT but only 33 (1.4%) submitted ACT, so the ACT percentiles rest on a very small group. Undergraduate enrollment (10,900) and the nonresident count (108) are the 'Total Undergraduates' figures in B1/B2.

cost.notes: First-year, full-time costs for the 2026-2027 academic year from the Common Data Set (G1, final figures; the 'not available' box is not ticked): New Hampshire-resident tuition $16,304, nonresident and international tuition $37,996, required fees $3,868, food and housing on campus $15,034 (housing $9,410 + meal plan $5,624). Estimated expenses (G5, residents): books $1,000, transportation $300, other $3,796 (other costs shown = transportation + other). Tuition varies by program (G4: 40.5% of undergraduates pay more): the university's international estimate of expenses for AY2026/27 (opened 2026-11-03) adds $1,504 for the College of Engineering & Physical Sciences and $1,452 for Paul College of Business & Economics. The same page lists mandatory student health insurance for F-1/J-1 students of $2,554 (shown as the international extra), total direct costs of $59,452 and a total estimated cost of attendance of $64,247 for undergraduates on the Durham campus (it uses miscellaneous expenses of $3,795).
